title: Question 10
stem: Two coils P and Q are placed close to one another, as shown in Fig. 10.1.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The current in coil P is constant.
An iron rod is inserted into coil P.
Explain why, during the time that the rod is moving, there is a reading on the voltmeter connected to coil Q.

markscheme_points.text: change of flux in coil Q causes induced e.m.f.

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: iron rod changes flux (density)/field; change of flux in coil Q causes induced e.m.f.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Magnetic fields and electromagnetic induction. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
iron rod changes flux (density)/field; change of flux in coil Q causes induced e.m.f.
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The current in coil P is now varied as shown in Fig. 10.2.
On Fig. 10.3, show the variation with time of the reading of the voltmeter connected to coil Q for time $t = 0$ to time $t = t_{2}$.

markscheme_points.text: constant reading (either polarity) from time zero to near t1
spike in one direction near t1 clearly showing a larger voltage
zero reading from near t1 to t2
